statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 18, at the upper end of the low band, with NQ futures at 29,240.00, down 208.75 points or 0.71%, printing the 29,238.75 low of a Globex session that opened at 29,458.50. E-mini S&P 500 futures are also on their session low at 7,630.25. Brent crude trades at 103.85, up 2.61% and close to its 104.01 session high, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.88% at a three-year high, and the VIX is at its session high of 16.99. That is coherent cross-asset alignment through an energy-to-rates channel with the index holding a session extreme, which is why tail has roughly doubled from the single-digit readings published earlier in the week. It remains below the block threshold because the moves are small in absolute terms, the VIX is still near 17, and yesterday's cash session reverted cleanly from its 29,334.40 low to a 29,421.55 close.
recommendation: Tail at 18 keeps the mapped policy state at EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window runs 12:30-14:30 UTC, covering the August PPI and jobless claims release, the pre-open repricing leg and the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open with its first full hour. That is where a hot producer-price print meeting an already one-way pre-market and a three-year-high long end is the most plausible route to repeated extension after failed retracements. Conditional tail inside the window reaches 22 and stays in the watch band rather than crossing the block threshold, consistent with the observation that large scheduled surprises have historically raised stress far more than they have produced a lethal no-retracement path. A secondary checkpoint sits at the 17:00 UTC 30-year bond auction.
headline: NQ sits on its 29,238.75 Globex low at 29,240.00 with Brent at 103.85 and the 10-year at a three-year-high 4.88%; tail rises to 18 and stress to 84 into the 12:30 UTC PPI print
body:
The Nasdaq-100 enters the August PPI release with the clearest one-way pre-market structure of the week. NQ futures trade at 29,240.00, down 208.75 points or 0.71%, having opened the Globex session at 29,458.50 and worked steadily lower into a 29,238.75 low that is effectively where price now sits. E-mini S&P 500 futures mirror it at 7,630.25 on their own 7,629.25 session low. Holding a session extreme rather than retracing from it is the single most relevant observation for a mean-reversion book, and it is the reason tail moves from the 7-9 readings published earlier in the week to 18.

The cross-asset picture is coherent rather than conflicting, which is what gives the structure weight. Brent crude is at 103.85, up 2.61%, near its 104.01 session high and extending a move that carried it through 100 for the first time since July during the previous session. WTI and Brent strength traces to a genuine geopolitical discontinuity: U.S. strikes on Iranian oil tankers, Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities and an Iranian strike on a U.S. base in Jordan, with Strait of Hormuz disruption now an active market concern. That energy impulse is transmitting directly into rates. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.88%, up 3.5 basis points and at its highest since October 2023, the 2-year is 4.47% and the 30-year is 5.32%. Futures markets have moved to price a meaningful probability of a Federal Reserve rate increase at the 15-16 September meeting, a repricing that was running near 60-68 percent in reporting from the previous session. The VIX at 16.99 is at its own session high and up 3.2 percent.

Set against that, several things argue for keeping tail below the block threshold. The absolute moves are modest: 0.71 percent on NQ, 0.18 percent on ES, and a VIX still under 17 is not the volatility signature of a market in disorderly repricing. Yesterday's cash session is the more instructive precedent. The Nasdaq-100 fell to 29,334.40 intraday and closed at 29,421.55, down only 0.29 percent, which is a clean demonstration that retracement was available even on a third consecutive down day with oil breaking 100. The danger window published in the previous assessment covered that cash open and passed without a pathological path.

August PPI and initial jobless claims are released at 12:30 UTC, inside the current clock-hour. Consensus looks for headline PPI at plus 0.4 percent month-on-month against a flat prior and core at plus 0.3 percent, with the annual rate expected to accelerate toward 5.3 percent. A print above that into an already directional tape and a three-year-high long end is the specific mechanism by which this session could deny meaningful retracement, and it is why conditional tail is lifted to 21 and 22 across the release and the 13:30 UTC cash open. It is not, however, treated as already observed: the assessment cutoff precedes the print, and event importance and forecast dispersion are scored into stress and confidence first. Stress at 84 is extreme and reflects oil above 103, a long end at multi-year highs, back-to-back inflation prints on consecutive days and unresolved geopolitical escalation. Confidence at 86 reflects live futures, oil, yield and volatility levels together with a calendar checked against the Federal Reserve's own meeting schedule.

One limitation is disclosed rather than smoothed over. No Claude assessment was published for any hour in the 24-hour lookback window, which runs from 12:00 UTC on 9 September to 11:00 UTC on 10 September. Every lookback slot is therefore marked unavailable. Past opinions are not reconstructed from information that only became available later, so the gap is reported as a gap.

The most recent published reading before the gap was generated at 09:34 UTC on 9 September and carried tail 8, stress 79, confidence 88 and a mixed dominant mode with the mapped state at EA_ON. Past assessments are not reconstructed using later information, so the interruption is reported rather than back-filled. For context drawn from market data rather than from published assessments, the 9 September cash session fell to 29,334.40 and closed at 29,421.55, down 0.29 percent, a third consecutive lower close that nonetheless retraced cleanly from its session low.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are framed by two Tier-1 U.S. inflation prints on consecutive days. August PPI and jobless claims arrive at 12:30 UTC inside the current clock-hour, and August CPI follows at 12:30 UTC on 11 September, just beyond the end of this window. Conditional tail peaks at 22 in the 13:00 UTC slot where the post-release repricing leg overlaps the U.S. cash open, holds the watch band at 21 and 20 for the release hour and the first full cash hour, and never approaches the block threshold. It then decays through the U.S. afternoon to a 10 overnight floor across the Asian session, before lifting again through the European morning to 16 in the final pre-CPI slot. Stress stays extreme at 84 to 87 across the release and cash open, eases to a 70 to 77 band overnight, and returns to 80 ahead of CPI. Secondary checkpoints inside the window are the 17:00 UTC 30-year bond auction, the 20:00 UTC cash close with Oracle results reported for after the bell, and the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen.
